title: Reusable predicate constants for eligible users

blocks.text: A rule used in more than one place belongs in a named constant, and named predicates combine into bigger ones: `IS_ADULT.and(IS_ACTIVE).and(HAS_VERIFIED_EMAIL)` reads as the rule it is.
The file declares `record User(String name, int age, boolean active, String email, boolean emailVerified)`. Fill in the constants of `UserFilters` and write one method:

rows: the email is not `null` (any non-null string counts, even a blank one) and it is verified
all three of the above hold
returns the names of the eligible users, in order

blocks.text: Building `IS_ELIGIBLE` from the other three with `and` keeps the rule in one place; the tests check what it accepts. Check the exact age at the boundary, an email that is missing, and a user who passes only some of the rules.

cases.says: Only adult, active users with a verified email are named, in order.
A user of exactly 18 is an adult.
A null email is not a verified email, whatever the verified flag says, in the constant and in eligibleNames alike.
IS_ELIGIBLE needs all three rules at once, a verified email included; passing some of them is not enough.

concepts: A rule used in many places becomes a named predicate constant, and constants combine with and.
